docs.title: BioPAT® Spectro UV Server Documentation
docs.text: Welcome to the BioPAT® Spectro UV Server documentation! This system provides real-time 201-wavelength UV-Vis spectroscopy acquisition and industrial OPC UA publication for Sartorius BioPAT® Spectro UV / tec5 spectrometers.

docs.title: What is BioPAT Spectro UV Server?
docs.text:
In industrial biomanufacturing and laboratory bioprocess monitoring, UV-Vis spectrometers capture continuous absorption curves across hundreds of wavelengths. However, standard automation setups usually constrain operators to extracting only 1 to 4 fixed wavelengths for DCS/SCADA historians.

BioPAT Spectro UV Server unlocks 201 simultaneous wavelengths (190 nm to 390 nm in 1 nm increments): - Direct UDP Ingestion: Captures high-frequency 840-byte UDP broadcasts from the tec5 spectrometer. - Microservices Architecture: Runs as a 3-container Docker stack (udpparser, redisserver, opcserver). - Industrial Standards Compliance: Publishes full spectral arrays over OPC UA (opc.tcp://<host>:4841) to SCADA, DeltaV, Ignition, or OSIsoft PI. - Hardware-Free Testing: Includes a mock UDP emitter to simulate full UV-Vis spectra with zero hardware attached.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The BioPAT® Spectro UV Server is designed around a decoupled, microservices architecture using Docker Compose and Redis as a real-time in-memory message bus.

docs.title: 1. Ingestion (udpparser)
docs.text:
• Binds to 0.0.0.0:20202 (UDP).
  • Receives 840-byte datagrams from the spectrometer.
  • Parses the 36-byte header: verifies length (840), extracts point count (201), wavelength bounds (190.0–390.0 nm), and data type code.
  • Unpacks 201 float32 values.
  • Writes JSON arrays into Redis with a 5-second TTL (ex=5) to prevent stale measurements if transmission ceases.

docs.title: 2. State & Message Bus (redisserver)
docs.text:
• Operates in-memory on port 6379.
  • Decouples high-frequency network packets from OPC UA client polling.

docs.title: 3. Industrial Publication (opcserver)
docs.text:
• Hosts standard OPC UA server on port 4841 (opc.tcp://0.0.0.0:4841).
  • Namespace: http://biopat/spectrouv.
  • Updates writable variables for each channel every 1 second.

docs.title: UDP Packet Structure (840 Bytes)
docs.text:
Offset (Bytes)  Size    Type     Description
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
0-3             4       bytes    Magic Header ID (0x08200000)
4-7             4       uint32   Header Info
8-11            4       uint32   Payload Length (840 bytes)
12-15           4       uint32   Padding / Reserved
16-17           2       uint16   Spectrum Type (4=sample, 5=reference, 9=absorbance)
18-19           2       uint16   Channel Index (1=channel 1, 2=channel 2)
20-23           4       float32  Start Wavelength (190.0 nm)
24-27           4       float32  End Wavelength (390.0 nm)
28-31           4       float32  Wavelength Step (1.0 nm)
32-35           4       uint32   Number of Points (201 points)
36-839          804     float32  201 × 4-byte little-endian IEEE-754 floats
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Total: 840 bytes

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This guide explains how to operate the BioPAT® Spectro UV Server, configure spectrometer UDP broadcasts, and consume live 201-wavelength data in industrial SCADA and PAT platforms.

docs.title: The 201-Wavelength UV Spectrum
docs.text:
The spectrometer measures optical signals from 190.0 nm to 390.0 nm in 1.0 nm increments, yielding an array of exactly 201 float32 values:

wavelength_nm = 190.0 + index

spectrum[0]    # 190.0 nm
spectrum[90]   # 280.0 nm (UV protein absorption peak)
spectrum[200]  # 390.0 nm

docs.title: Data Types
docs.text:
The spectrometer emits several spectral data types, each mapped to a specific tec5 type identifier:

Data Type Packet Type Redis Key OPC UA Tag Description Absorbance 9 absorbance_channel_1 absorbance_channel_1 Optical Absorbance ($A$) across 201 wavelengths Sample Intensity 4 sample_channel_1 sample_channel_1 Raw measurement intensity counts ($I$) Reference Intensity 5 onlinereference_channel_1 onlinereference_channel_1 Baseline reference intensity counts ($I_0$) Transmission 7 transmission_channel_1 transmission_channel_1 Transmittance ratio ($I / I_0$) Calibration 11 calibration_channel_1 calibration_channel_1 Dark / factory calibration baseline Wavelengths Axis wavelengths_channel_1 Wavelength Axis array [190.0, 191.0, ..., 390.0]

docs.title: Connecting OPC UA Clients
docs.text: The OPC UA server listens on opc.tcp://<host>:4841 under namespace index 1 (http://biopat/spectrouv).

docs.title: Python Client Example (asyncua)
docs.text:
import asyncio
from asyncua import Client

async def read_spectrum():
    url = "opc.tcp://localhost:4841"
    async with Client(url=url) as client:
        # Access Channel 1 Absorbance variable node
        node = client.get_node("ns=1;s=absorbance_channel_1")
        absorbance_values = await node.read_value()

        # Access Wavelength axis
        wl_node = client.get_node("ns=1;s=Wavelength")
        wavelengths = await wl_node.read_value()

        print(f"Acquired {len(absorbance_values)} wavelength points:")
        print(f"  {wavelengths[90]} nm: {absorbance_values[90]:.4f} AU")

asyncio.run(read_spectrum())

docs.title: SCADA & Bioreactor Systems (Ignition, DeltaV, PCS 7)
docs.text:
1. Add an OPC UA connection to opc.tcp://<server_ip>:4841 (Security: None / Anonymous or configured).
  2. Browse to Objects -> spectrouv_1.
  3. Map absorbance_channel_1 as a 201-element float array tag.

docs.title: Testing with Mock Emitter
docs.text:
When testing without a physical spectrometer attached:

python -m parselibrary.mock_udp_emitter --host 127.0.0.1 --port 20202

This broadcasts authentic 840-byte UDP packets containing simulated protein absorbance peaks at 280 nm.

docs.title: Quick Start Guide
docs.text: Get the BioPAT® Spectro UV Server running and publishing live 201-wavelength data in under 2 minutes!

docs.title: 1. Start the Docker Stack
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/Sir-Narwhal/biopat-spectrouv-server-1.git
cd biopat-spectrouv-server-1

docker compose up -d

Verify that all three containers are healthy: 

docker compose ps

docs.title: 2. Test with Simulated Spectra (No Hardware Needed)
docs.text:
Launch the simulated UDP emitter:

python -m parselibrary.mock_udp_emitter

You will see output showing periodic cycles of Reference, Sample Intensity, and Absorbance packets being transmitted to port 20202: 

[Mock Emitter] Broadcasting mock UDP spectral data to 127.0.0.1:20202...
[Mock Emitter] Cycle 1: Broadcasted sample, reference, and absorbance (201 wavelengths @ 190-390 nm)

docs.title: 3. Connect Your OPC UA Client
docs.text:
Connect to: 

opc.tcp://localhost:4841

In your OPC UA client (such as UaExpert): 1. Navigate to: Root -> Objects -> spectrouv_1. 2. Drag absorbance_channel_1, sample_channel_1, or Wavelength into the Data Access View. 3. Observe live array updates in real-time!

docs.title: Deployment Modes
docs.text: BioPAT® Spectro UV Server can be deployed in two modes: 1. Containerized (Recommended): Using Docker Compose. 2. Native: Running Python processes directly on the host.

docs.title: Configuration (.env)
docs.text:
Create a .env file in the project root:

cp .env.example .env

Default settings: 

UDP_IP=0.0.0.0
UDP_PORT=20202
UDP_CHANNEL_NAME=channel_1

OPC_IP_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0
OPC_PORT_NUMBER=4841

REDIS_IP_ADDRESS=redisserver
REDIS_PORT_NUMBER=6379

docs.title: Launching Services
docs.text:
# Start in background
docker compose up -d

# View logs
docker compose logs -f udpparser
docker compose logs -f opcserver

# Stop services
docker compose down

docs.title: Port Mappings
docs.text:
Ensure the following firewall ports are open on the server host:

Port Protocol Service Description 20202 UDP udpparser Receives spectrometer UDP broadcast 4841 TCP opcserver OPC UA server endpoint for SCADA clients 6379 TCP redisserver Internal Redis state bus

docs.title: Issue: udpparser shows socket timeout or receives no packets
docs.text:
[UDP Parser] Socket timeout waiting for UDP broadcast; retrying...

Causes: 1. The spectrometer host PC is sending UDP packets to a different IP or port. 2. A firewall is blocking UDP port 20202.

Solutions: - Verify the spectrometer PC is configured to send UDP packets to the IP of the server on port 20202. - Check if port 20202 is open and listening: 

# Windows
netstat -ano | findstr :20202
# Linux
ss -ulpn | grep 20202
- Send a test packet using the mock emitter: 
python -m parselibrary.mock_udp_emitter --host 127.0.0.1 --port 20202

docs.title: Error: redis.exceptions.ConnectionError
docs.text:
redis.exceptions.ConnectionError: Error 111 connecting to localhost:6379

Solutions: 1. Verify the Redis container is running: 

docker compose ps redisserver
2. Test connection with redis-cli: 
docker compose exec redisserver redis-cli ping
# Expected: PONG
3. Inspect keys currently stored in Redis: 
docker compose exec redisserver redis-cli keys "*"

docs.title: Issue: Client connects but variables read [0.0, 0.0, ...]
docs.text:
Causes: - No UDP packets have been received in the last 5 seconds (keys expired in Redis). - udpparser is not running or connected to a different Redis instance.

Solutions: 1. Check udpparser logs: 

docker compose logs -f udpparser
2. Check if keys exist in Redis: 
docker compose exec redisserver redis-cli get absorbance_channel_1
3. Start the mock emitter to verify the pipeline: 
python -m parselibrary.mock_udp_emitter

docs.title: 4. Port Conflicts
docs.text:
If port 4841 (OPC UA) or 20202 (UDP) is already in use by another application: 1. Open .env. 2. Change the host port mappings: 

UDP_PORT=20205
OPC_PORT_NUMBER=4845
3. Restart Docker Compose: 
docker compose up -d

docs.title: Module: parselibrary.mock_udp_emitter
docs.text: Testing utility for broadcasting synthetic 840-byte tec5 UDP datagrams without physical spectrometer hardware.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: python -m parselibrary.mock_udp_emitter --host 127.0.0.1 --port 20202 --interval 1.0

docs.text:

docs.title: Module: parselibrary.opcua_server
docs.text: This module implements an OPC UA server that publishes UV-Vis spectral data for real-time access by industrial control systems and SCADA platforms.

docs.title: Function: opcua_loop()
docs.text: async def opcua_loop(redis_server: redis.Redis) -> None:

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Run the OPC UA server and continuously publish spectral data from Redis to connected SCADA clients.

Creates an OPC UA server with a BioPal SpectraUV namespace containing two spectrometer channels (spectrouv_1, spectrouv_2). Each channel exposes five spectral data types (transmission, absorbance, reference, sample, calibration) plus a wavelength axis. The server polls Redis every 1 second for updated spectral values and pushes them to OPC UA clients, enabling real-time subscription and monitoring.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: redis_server: redis.Redis - An active Redis connection (authenticated and validated) - Port: 6379 (default) or as configured - Must have decode_responses=True for string operations - Example: redis.Redis(host="localhost", port=6379, decode_responses=True)

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: None - Function runs indefinitely until process termination - Blocks the calling coroutine

docs.title: Behavior
docs.text:
The function executes an infinite async loop with these steps:

  1. Initialization (runs once)
  2. Creates OPC UA Server instance
  3. Registers BioPal SpectraUV namespace
  4. Creates two channel objects (spectrouv_1, spectrouv_2)
  5. For each channel and datatype, creates writable OPC UA variables

  6. Creates read-only wavelength axis variable (190-391 nm)

  7. Polling Loop (repeats every 1 second)

  8. Scans Redis for keys matching patterns: transmission*, absorbance*, etc.
  9. For each key found:
    • Retrieves JSON-encoded spectral data from Redis
    • Identifies target channel (channel_1 or channel_2)
    • Updates corresponding OPC UA variable with new values
  10. Sleeps 1 second before next poll
  11. Catches and logs exceptions (continues operating if errors occur)

docs.title: OPC UA Namespace Structure
docs.text:
ns=1 (BioPal SpectraUV)
├── spectrouv_1 (Object)
│   ├── transmission_channel_1 (Variable, 201 floats)
│   ├── absorbance_channel_1 (Variable, 201 floats)
│   ├── onlinereference_channel_1 (Variable, 201 floats)
│   ├── sample_channel_1 (Variable, 201 floats)
│   ├── calibration_channel_1 (Variable, 201 floats)
│   └── Wavelength (Variable, 201 floats, read-only)
└── spectrouv_2 (Object)
    ├── transmission_channel_2 (Variable, 201 floats)
    ├── absorbance_channel_2 (Variable, 201 floats)
    ├── onlinereference_channel_2 (Variable, 201 floats)
    ├── sample_channel_2 (Variable, 201 floats)
    ├── calibration_channel_2 (Variable, 201 floats)
    └── Wavelength (Variable, 201 floats, read-only)

docs.title: Data Type Definitions
docs.text:
Each datatype variable contains 201 floating-point values:

Datatype Meaning Source transmission Raw transmission spectrum (I/I₀) Direct measurement absorbance Calculated absorbance (A = -log₁₀T) Derived from transmission onlinereference Reference/calibration spectrum Stored calibration sample Active sample measurement Current measurement calibration Calibration data used Reference baseline

docs.title: Wavelength Axis
docs.text:
• 201 values from 190.0 to 390.0 nm
  • Spacing: 1.0 nm between consecutive values
  • Read-only: Cannot be modified via OPC UA clients

docs.title: Redis Key Naming Convention
docs.text:
The server scans Redis for keys following this pattern:

{datatype}_{channel}

Examples:
transmission_channel_1
absorbance_channel_2
onlinereference_channel_1

Valid pattern components:

Component Valid Values {datatype} transmission, absorbance, onlinereference, sample, calibration {channel} channel_1, channel_2

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Configuration is via environment variables:

REDIS_IP_ADDRESS = os.environ.get("REDIS_IP_ADDRESS", "10.20.20.11")
REDIS_PORT_NUMBER = int(os.environ.get("REDIS_PORT_NUMBER", 6379))
OPC_IP_ADDRESS = os.environ.get("OPC_IP_ADDRESS", "0.0.0.0")
OPC_PORT_NUMBER = int(os.environ.get("OPC_PORT_NUMBER", 4841))
Variable Default Purpose REDIS_IP_ADDRESS 10.20.20.11 Redis host IP REDIS_PORT_NUMBER 6379 Redis port OPC_IP_ADDRESS 0.0.0.0 OPC UA listen address (0.0.0.0 = all interfaces) OPC_PORT_NUMBER 4841 OPC UA port (standard)

docs.title: Exceptions & Error Handling
docs.text:
The function catches and logs exceptions internally, allowing the server to continue operating even if errors occur:

Common exceptions:

Exception Cause Recovery redis.ConnectionError Redis unavailable Retries next poll json.JSONDecodeError Invalid JSON in Redis Logs warning, skips key KeyError Channel not recognized Logs warning, skips value Exception General error Logged, server continues

All exceptions are logged via Python logging at WARNING level.

docs.title: Basic Startup
docs.text:
import redis
import asyncio
from parselibrary.opcua_server import opcua_loop

async def main():
    # Connect to Redis
    r = redis.Redis(host='localhost', port=6379, decode_responses=True)

    # Run OPC UA server
    await opcua_loop(r)

# Run forever
asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Command-line Execution
docs.text:
# With environment variables
export REDIS_IP_ADDRESS=192.168.1.10
export OPC_PORT_NUMBER=8841
python -m parselibrary.opcua_server

docs.title: Docker Container
docs.text:
FROM python:3.11-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt
COPY parselibrary/ parselibrary/
ENV REDIS_IP_ADDRESS=redis
ENV OPC_IP_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0
CMD ["python", "-m", "parselibrary.opcua_server"]

docs.title: Publishing Data to Redis
docs.text:
import json
import redis
from parselibrary.parsing_spectra import parsebinary

# Parse spectrum
spectrum = parsebinary("/data/sample.bin")

# Connect to Redis
r = redis.Redis(decode_responses=True)

# Publish to Redis for OPC UA server to read
r.set("transmission_channel_1", json.dumps(list(spectrum)))

# Server will pick this up in next polling cycle (~1 second)
print("Spectrum published")

docs.title: Connecting OPC UA Client
docs.text:
import asyncio
from asyncua import Client

async def connect():
    client = Client("opc.tcp://localhost:4841")
    async with client:
        # Browse namespace
        root = client.get_root_node()
        objects = await root.get_children()

        # Get transmission data for channel 1
        node = client.get_node("ns=1;s=transmission_channel_1")
        value = await node.read_value()

        print(f"Got {len(value)} wavelength points")
        print(f"First 5 values: {value[:5]}")

        # Subscribe to changes
        async def on_change(node, var):
            print(f"Value changed: {var}")

        handler = await node.subscribe_value(on_change)

        # Keep connection open
        await asyncio.sleep(10)

asyncio.run(connect())

docs.title: Performance Characteristics
docs.text:
• Polling latency: ~1 second (configurable in source code, line 106)
  • OPC UA update frequency: 1 Hz
  • Redis scan time: ~5-50 ms per poll (depends on key count)
  • Memory overhead: ~5 MB for 2 channels × 5 datatypes × 201 values
  • Max concurrent clients: 10-50 (asyncio limited)

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
Events are logged at level WARNING (configured in source):

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.WARNING)

Change level for more verbose output:

import logging
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG)

docs.title: Module: parselibrary.parsing_spectra
docs.text: This module provides functions for parsing binary UV-Vis spectral data files.

docs.title: Function: parsebinary()
docs.text: def parsebinary(binfile: str) -> Tuple[float, ...]:

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Parse a binary spectral data file (.bin) and extract absorption values.

Reads a binary file containing UV-Vis spectral data with magic byte markers, validates file integrity, skips metadata, and extracts floating-point absorption values for wavelengths in the UV range (190-391 nm).

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: binfile: str - Absolute path to the binary .bin file to parse - Example: "/data/spectra/spectrum_001.bin"

docs.title: Returns
docs.text: Tuple[float, ...] - Tuple of 201 floating-point numbers representing absorption values - Index maps to wavelength: wavelength_nm = 190 + index - Values are unitless absorption coefficients (typically 0.0 to 2.5)

docs.title: Raises
docs.text:
ValueError - Raised if file does not have correct magic byte markers (0xEFBEADDE) at start and end - Indicates corrupted, incomplete, or incorrect file format - Message: "Bad file markers"

FileNotFoundError - Raised if the specified file does not exist

IOError - Raised if file cannot be read due to permissions or I/O errors

docs.title: File Format Requirements
docs.text:
Input file must follow exact binary format:

Byte Range    Size    Content
────────────────────────────────────
0-3           4       Magic marker: 0xEFBEADDE
4-79          76      Metadata (file header, not parsed)
80-883        804     Spectral data (201 × 4-byte float32, little-endian)
884-887       4       Magic marker: 0xEFBEADDE

Total:        888 bytes

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
from parselibrary.parsing_spectra import parsebinary

# Parse a spectrum file
spectrum = parsebinary("/data/sample_001.bin")

# Access wavelength data
print(f"190 nm: {spectrum[0]:.4f}")     # First value
print(f"290 nm: {spectrum[100]:.4f}")   # Middle value
print(f"390 nm: {spectrum[200]:.4f}")   # Last value

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
from parselibrary.parsing_spectra import parsebinary

try:
    spectrum = parsebinary("/data/corrupted.bin")
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("File not found")
except ValueError as e:
    print(f"Invalid spectrum file: {e}")

docs.title: Processing Multiple Files
docs.text:
import os
from parselibrary.parsing_spectra import parsebinary

spectrum_dir = "/data/spectra"
spectra = {}

for filename in os.listdir(spectrum_dir):
    if not filename.endswith('.bin'):
        continue

    try:
        path = os.path.join(spectrum_dir, filename)
        spectrum = parsebinary(path)
        spectra[filename] = spectrum
        print(f"✓ Loaded {filename}")
    except (ValueError, FileNotFoundError) as e:
        print(f"✗ Failed {filename}: {e}")

print(f"Loaded {len(spectra)} spectra")

docs.title: Integration with OPC UA
docs.text:
import json
import redis
from parselibrary.parsing_spectra import parsebinary

# Parse and publish to Redis for OPC UA server
spectrum = parsebinary("/data/sample.bin")

# Store as JSON for Redis
r = redis.Redis(decode_responses=True)
r.set("transmission_channel_1", json.dumps(list(spectrum)))

# OPC UA server will read this and publish via OPC UA
print("Spectrum published to Redis")

docs.title: Performance Notes
docs.text:
• Parsing time: ~1-5 ms per file (single-threaded)
  • Memory usage: ~2 KB per spectrum tuple (201 floats)
  • Throughput: Can parse ~100-200 files/second with asyncio

docs.title: Wavelength Mapping
docs.text:
The returned tuple maps directly to wavelengths:

Index Wavelength (nm) 0 190 1 191 ... ... 100 290 ... ... 200 390

docs.title: Data Type Details
docs.text:
• Values: Single-precision floating-point (32-bit)
  • Byte order: Little-endian (standard Intel/x86)
  • Range: Typically 0.0 to 2.5 (absorption coefficient)
  • Precision: ~6 significant decimal digits

docs.title: Module: parselibrary.udp_parser
docs.text: The UDP Parser service receives, validates, and decodes incoming 840-byte UDP spectral broadcast datagrams from the spectrometer.

docs.title: unpack_udp(binary_string: bytes) -> List[float]
docs.text: Extracts the 201 float32 values from an incoming 840-byte datagram payload.

docs.title: collect_mpt_spectra(udp: socket.socket) -> Dict[str, List[float]]
docs.text: Reads datagrams from the UDP socket and maps tec5 packet type integers to spectral identifiers: - Type 4 $ ightarrow$ sample (Sample Intensity) - Type 5 $ ightarrow$ onlinereference (Reference Intensity) - Type 7 $ ightarrow$ transmission - Type 9 $ ightarrow$ absorbance - Type 11 $ ightarrow$ calibration
